Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY DILG Legal opini n OCT 6 s. 2011 MAYOR JAKCSON CINCO DY Municipality of Roxas Province of Oriental Mindoro Dear Mayor Dy: This has reference to your letter dated 05 September 2011 informing the Department that Barangay Morente which used to be a part of Bongabong town is now considered under the jurisdiction of your town per Board Resolution No. 1259- 2011 of the current Sangguniang Panlalawigan (SP) of Oriental Mindoro affirming Provincial Board Resolution No. 238 dated October 03, 1966 deciding the inclusion of the said barangay to your town. In view of the foregoing, you are now requesting the Department to cawse the implementation of the decisions/resolutions of the past and present SP of the Province of Oriental Mindoro. In reply to your request, please be informed that this Department has already addressed a similar request in DILG Opinion No. 37, series of 2008. In the said Opinion, we opined that the DILG's role in decisions rendered by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan pertaining to boundary disputes, WOUId only be that of an official custodian of documents relative to the dispute citing therein Article 17 (h) and Article 19 of the Rules and Regulations Implementing the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 71 60), which provide and we quote: "(h) Decision — Within sixty (60) days from the date the certification was issued, the dispute shaZZ be formaZty tried and decided by the sanggunian concerned. Copies of the decision shaZZ, within fifteen (15) days from the promulgation thereof, be furnished the parties concerned, DILG, ZocaZ assessor, Comelec, NSO, and other NGAs concerned." "ART. 19. Official Custodian.—The DILG shaZZ be the official custodian of copies of azz documents on boundary disputes of LGUs." We have attached a photocopy of the aforesaid DILG Opinion No. 37, series Of for YOLJr ready reference. Thank you. Very YOU r S, AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary Y Ls/17

Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT or THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT Francisco Gold Condominium II, EDSA cor. Mapagmahal St. Diliman, Quezon City 27 May 2008 DIRECTOR LUIS l. DANAO DILG Provincial Field Office Bayombong, Nueva Vizcaya Dear Director Danao: This refers to your letter-request for a Department Advisory regarding Resolution No. 2008-598 dated 30 April 2008 issued by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Nueva Vizcaya, resolving the boundary dispute between the Municipalities of Aritao and Sta. Fe, Province of Nueva Vizcaya, the last paragraph thereof reads as follows: "RESOLVED, FURTHER, that this Resolution be forwarded to the DILG Provincial Office for the implementation of the same based on the 1987 Constitution and RA 7160, to the Honorable Governor Luisa LZoren Cuaresma, Honorable Mayor Lucita L. Tan, Honorable Florante S. Gerdan, the respective Sangguniang Bayan of the two municipalities and their counsels, for their information and guidance. " Your query is basically an inquiry as to whether or not the Department, through your office, can implement the said Resolution based on the abovecited paragraph. Article 17 (h) of the Rules and Regulations Implementing the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160) provides in full: "(h) Decision — Within sixty (60) days from the date the certification was issued, the dispute shall be formaZZy tried and decided by the sanggunian concerned. Copies of the decision shall, within fifteen (15) days from the promulgation thereof, be furnished the parties concerned, DILG, ZocaZ assessor, Come Zec, NSO, and other NGAs concerned. " Parenthetically, Article 19 of the same Implementing Rules and Regulations provides: "ART. 19. Official Custodian.- The DILG shaZZ be the official custodian of copies of au documents on boundary disputes of LGUs. "

2- It is, therefore, evident from the aforequoted provisions that the DILGs role in decisions rendered by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan pertaining to boundary disputes, would only be that of an official custodian of documents relative to the dispute. Nowhere in the Local Government Code of 1991 or its Implementing Rules and Regulations mandate the Department to implement decisions pertaining to boundary disputes. Along this line, you are hereby advised to inform the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Nueva Vizcaya of the Department's role on the matter as aforestated and to further inform the said Sanggunian that in implementing its decision, Article 17 (h) of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of the Local Government Code requires them to immediately furnish the parties concerned copy of the decision. The parties concerned are immediately furnished copy of the decision so that they may, within the prescriptive period, still exercise available legal remedies, such as an appeal before the Regional Trial Court having jurisdiction over the area in dispute as provided for in Section 119 of the Local Government Code. In addition, if the period within which to file an appeal has lapsed, i.e. fifteen (15) days from notice of judgment, and no appeal pursuant to Section 119 of the Local Government Code was filed by either party before the concerned Regional Trial Court, the Sangguian shall accordingly officially furnish the Provincial Assessor, the COMELEC, National Statistics Office, DILG, LMB-DENR and DBM and such other national government agencies concerned, copy of the final decision for the correction of their records under their respective custody. Please be guided accordingly. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADE O Acting Secretarv C/ Legal:87/La cc: Director Renato L. Brion DILG Regional Office No. 02 Tuguegarao City
